why: A range sum from a running prefix: the left sum of index i is the prefix before i, and the right sum is total - left - values[i]. One pass with a running prefix answers each index in O(1) instead of re-adding both sides.
hints: Computing the left and right sums from scratch for every index is O(n^2). What single number makes the right sum free once you know the left sum?
The total. Right sum = total - leftSum - values[i].
total = sum(values); left = 0; for each i check left == total - left - values[i], then left += values[i]. Return the first hit, else -1. O(n).
pitfalls: The value at i belongs to neither side.
Index 0 has left sum 0; the last index has right sum 0.
Return the LEFTMOST index; return -1 for an empty array.
